46: /*
47:  * Coexistence netif wire id (2-bit co_hdr.vif_idx). Roles are NOT pinned to a
48:  * fixed LMAC VIF index any more (P2P GO/GC float on vif0/vif1 so the MCC
49:  * channel scheduler can handle them). We therefore key the wire id off the
50:  * (netif type, p2p) role instead of the LMAC index:
51:  *
52:  *   wire 0 = infra STA   (STA-type, !p2p) -> host g_mlan
53:  *   wire 1 = SoftAP      (AP-type,  !p2p) -> host g_uap
54:  *   wire 2 = P2P GO      (AP-type,   p2p) -> host g_p2p_go
55:  *   wire 3 = P2P GC      (STA-type,  p2p) -> host g_p2p_gc
56:  *
57:  * The TX path is symmetric: host tags the wire id, CP maps it back to the
58:  * current LMAC VIF index via cif_wire_to_lmac_vif() (no longer identity).
59:  */
60: static uint8_t cif_vif_to_netif_wire(void *vif)
61: {
62:     netif_if_t t = wifi_netif_vif_to_netif_type(vif);
63:     bool p2p = cif_vif_is_p2p(vif);
64: 
65:     if ((t == NETIF_IF_AP) && p2p)
66:         return 2;
67:     if ((t == NETIF_IF_STA) && p2p)
68:         return 3;
69: 
70:     return (uint8_t)t;
71: }
72: 
73: /*
74:  * Reverse of cif_vif_to_netif_wire(): map a host wire id back to the LMAC VIF
75:  * index currently held by that role. Since GO/GC float on vif0/vif1, the old
76:  * identity mapping (wire==index) no longer holds, so look the role up in the
77:  * active VIF table. Falls back to the wire id if no active match is found.
78:  */
79: static uint8_t cif_wire_to_lmac_vif(uint8_t wire)
80: {
81:     netif_if_t want_type;
82:     bool want_p2p;
83: 
84:     switch (wire)
85:     {
86:         case 0: want_type = NETIF_IF_STA; want_p2p = false; break;
87:         case 1: want_type = NETIF_IF_AP;  want_p2p = false; break;
88:         case 2: want_type = NETIF_IF_AP;  want_p2p = true;  break;
89:         case 3: want_type = NETIF_IF_STA; want_p2p = true;  break;
90:         default: return wire;
91:     }
92: 
93:     for (void *vif = mac_vif_mgmt_first_vif(); vif != NULL;
94:          vif = mac_vif_mgmt_next_vif(vif))
95:     {
96:         if ((wifi_netif_vif_to_netif_type(vif) == want_type) &&
97:             (cif_vif_is_p2p(vif) == want_p2p))
98:             return wifi_netif_vif_to_vifid(vif);
99:     }
100: 
101:     return wire;
102: }

104: static uint8_t cif_vif_id_route()

106:     uint8_t sta_vif_id = vif_mgmt_get_sta_vif_index();
107:     uint8_t sap_vif_id = vif_mgmt_get_softap_vif_index();
108:     uint8_t ap_id = INVALID_STA_IDX;
109:     void *vif = NULL;
110: 
111:     if ((sta_vif_id != INVALID_VIF_IDX) && (sap_vif_id != INVALID_VIF_IDX))
112:     {
113:         vif = mac_vif_mgmt_get_entry(sta_vif_id);
114:         if (vif)
115:             ap_id = mac_vif_mgmt_get_u_sta_ap_id(vif);
116: 
117:         if (ap_id != INVALID_STA_IDX)
118:         {
119:             return sta_vif_id + 0xF;
120:         }
121:         else
122:         {
123:             return sap_vif_id + 0xF;
124:         }
125:     }
126:     else if ((sta_vif_id != INVALID_VIF_IDX) && (sap_vif_id == INVALID_VIF_IDX))
127:     {

129:     }

131:     {
132:         return sap_vif_id + 0xF;
133:     }
134: 
135:     return INVALID_VIF_IDX;
136: }

138: bk_err_t cif_handle_txdata(void *head)
139: {
140:     uint8_t ret = BK_OK;
141:     struct pbuf* pbuf = NULL;
142: 
143:     cpdu_t* cpdu = (cpdu_t*)head;
144:     /* Map the host wire id (0..3) to the LMAC VIF index this role currently
145:      * holds (P2P GO/GC float on vif0/vif1), then tag it with the +0xF offset
146:      * the downstream TX path expects. */
147:     uint8_t vif_id = cif_wire_to_lmac_vif(cpdu->co_hdr.vif_idx) + 0xF;
148:     BK_ASSERT(vif_id < 19);
149: #if CONFIG_BK_RAW_LINK
150:     if (cpdu->co_hdr.special_type == TX_RAW_LINK_TYPE)
151:     {
152:         struct ctrl_cmd_hdr *cpdu = (struct ctrl_cmd_hdr*)head;
153:         uint32_t align_mac_len = CIF_RAW_LINK_MEM_ALIGN_SIZE(RLK_WIFI_MAC_ADDR_LEN);
154: 
155:         if (cpdu->msg_hdr.id == RLK_TX_SEND_EVT)
156:         {
157:              ret = bk_rlk_send((uint8_t *)head + sizeof(struct ctrl_cmd_hdr), 
158:                     (uint8_t *)head + sizeof(struct ctrl_cmd_hdr) + align_mac_len, cpdu->co_hdr.length);
159: 
160:             cpdu->co_hdr.special_type = TX_RLK_FREE_MEM_TYPE;
161:             // Notify AP side to free memory instead of freeing on CP side
162:             cif_send_mem_free_req(head);
163:         }
164: 
165:         return ret;
166:     }
167: #endif
168: 
169:     pbuf = (struct pbuf*)((uint8_t*)head - sizeof(struct pbuf));
170: #if CONFIG_CONTROLLER_RX_DIRECT_PSH
171:     if(cpdu->co_hdr.need_free)
172:     {
173:         cif_stats_ptr->cif_rxc_cnt++;
174:         CIF_LOGV("%s free p:%x,p->ref:%d\r\n",__func__, pbuf,pbuf->ref);
175:         pbuf->ref--;
176:         pbuf_free(pbuf);
177:         return BK_OK;
178:     }
179: #endif
180: 
181:     CIF_STATS_INC(buf_in_txdata);
182:     cif_stats_ptr->cif_tx_cnt++;
183:     CIF_LOGV("%s p:%x next:%x payload%x sizeof:%d\r\n",__func__, pbuf, pbuf->next, pbuf->payload, sizeof(struct pbuf));
184:     CIF_LOGV("%s p:%x,vif_id=%d\r\n",__func__, pbuf,vif_id);
185: 
186: #if CONFIG_CONTROLLER_DEBUG
187:     TRACK_PBUF_ALLOC(pbuf);
188: #endif
189: 
190: #if CONFIG_CONTROLLER_AP_BUFFER_COPY
191:     /*
192:      * In bridge mode AP-side bridgeif_send_to_port() already pbuf_clone's into
193:      * a PBUF_RAW_TX TX-headroom buffer (see bridgeif.c:1386). Cloning again on
194:      * CP wastes ~1.5KB heap per frame and serializes TX. Skip the second clone
195:      * when bridge is ENABLED and pass the pbuf to bmsg_tx_sender directly.
196:      */
197: #if CONFIG_BRIDGE
198:     if (bk_wifi_get_bridge_state() == BRIDGE_STATE_ENABLED)
199:     {
200:         ret = bmsg_tx_sender(pbuf, vif_id);
201:         if (ret != BK_OK)
202:         {
203:             cif_free_ap_txbuf(pbuf);
204:             ret = false;
205:         }
206:         return ret;
207:     }
208: #endif
209: 
210:     struct pbuf* p_copy = pbuf_clone(PBUF_RAW_TX,PBUF_RAM,pbuf);
211: 
212:     if((p_copy == NULL) || (p_copy->payload == NULL))
213:     {
214:         cif_free_ap_txbuf(pbuf);
215:         return BK_OK;
216:     }
217: 
218:     memcpy((void*)(p_copy+1),(void*)(pbuf+1),sizeof(cpdu_t));
219:     cif_free_ap_txbuf(pbuf);
220:     ret = bmsg_tx_sender(p_copy, vif_id);
221: 
222:     if(ret != BK_OK)
223:     {
224:         //CIF_LOGE("%s %d,p:0x%x\r\n",__func__,__LINE__,p_copy);
225:         pbuf_free(p_copy);
226:     }
227: 
228: #else
229:     ret = bmsg_tx_sender(pbuf, vif_id);
230:     if(ret != BK_OK)
231:     {
232:         cif_free_ap_txbuf(pbuf);
233:         ret = false;
234:     }
235: #endif
236:     return ret;
237: }

text:
**Smallest Patch**

Add the same opt-in symbol to both core Kconfig trees. It must be independently enabled because AP and CP generate separate `sdkconfig.h` files.

```kconfig
config WIFI_VNET_AP_IPV4
	bool "Application core owns VNET IPv4"
	depends on WIFI_VNET_CONTROLLER && CONTROLLER_RX_DIRECT_PSH
	default n
	help
	  Forward VNET IPv4 and ARP to the application core. The controller
	  retains Wi-Fi radio, association, security, and EAPOL handling.
```

Place it after `CONTROLLER_RX_DIRECT_PSH` in:

- [CP controller Kconfig](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/components/controller_if/Kconfig:5)
- [AP Wi-Fi driver Kconfig](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/bk_wifi_driver/Kconfig:5)

Enable `CONFIG_WIFI_VNET_AP_IPV4=y` in both active project configs:

- [CP app config](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/projects/app/cp/config/bk7258/config:441)
- [AP app config](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/projects/app/ap/config/bk7258_ap/config:653)

Mirror it into both `no_cli.config` files if that build variant is used. Do not patch generated files under `build/`.

**CP IPv4 Stack**

At entry to `sta_ip_down()` and `sta_ip_start()` in [CP net.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/components/lwip_intf_v2_1/lwip-2.1.2/port/net.c:629):

```c
#if CONFIG_WIFI_VNET_AP_IPV4
	return;
#endif
```

Guarding the functions, rather than only [bk_netif.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/components/bk_netif/bk_netif.c:30), covers the numerous direct callers in `wifi_v2.c`, `wifi_wpa_cmd.c`, `ctrl_iface.c`, and controller commands.

Also put the same early return in `net_begin_send_arp_reply()` at [CP net.c:1382](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/components/lwip_intf_v2_1/lwip-2.1.2/port/net.c:1382). Otherwise the Wi-Fi 6 power-save indication can still invoke CP `etharp_reply()` using retained/fast-DHCP state.

**RX Ownership**

In [cif_wifi_dp.c:465](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/components/controller_if/cif_wifi_dp.c:465), make ARP AP-exclusive before the existing direct-push branch:

```c
#if CONFIG_WIFI_VNET_AP_IPV4
	p_copy = p;
	upload2ctrl = false;
#elif CONFIG_CONTROLLER_RX_DIRECT_PSH
	/* existing direct-push ARP code */
#else
	/* existing copied ARP code */
#endif
```

Thus both ARP requests and replies go to AP, not the current request-only/AP plus reply-both behavior.

At [cif_wifi_dp.c:554](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/components/controller_if/cif_wifi_dp.c:554), replace the filter decision with:

```c
#if CONFIG_WIFI_VNET_AP_IPV4
	bool forward_to_ap = true;
#else
	bool forward_to_ap = !cif_filter_check_ip_data(p);
#endif

if (forward_to_ap) {
	/* existing forwarding body from the current false branch */
} else {
	upload2ctrl = true;
}
```

This forwards DHCP, DNS, ICMP, IGMP, TCP, UDP, local-port traffic, and other IPv4 protocols. Leave [the `ETHTYPE_EAPOL` case](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/components/controller_if/cif_wifi_dp.c:459) unchanged so EAPOL remains on CP.

**Link Events**

In `wpas_notify_connected()` at [notify.c:373](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/components/wpa_supplicant-2.10/wpa_supplicant/notify.c:373), after the existing GC notification, add:

```c
#if CONFIG_WIFI_VNET_AP_IPV4
#if CONFIG_P2P
	if (!wpas_use_p2p_gc_netif(wpa_s))
#endif
		cif_handle_bk_cmd_wifi_event_ind(CIF_WIFI_EVT_STA_CONNECTED,
						&sta_connected,
						sizeof(sta_connected));
#endif
```

For disconnect at [notify.c:395](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/components/wpa_supplicant-2.10/wpa_supplicant/notify.c:395), move initialization of `sta_disconnected` and the existing `cif_handle_bk_cmd_wifi_event_ind(...DISCONNECTED...)` block to immediately after `mhdr_set_station_status(state)`, before the auto-reconnect gate. Keep only CP’s local `bk_event_post()` inside that gate. Otherwise AP can retain DHCP/netif state during a real link loss while CP reconnects.

No AP controller-event change is needed: [wdrv_cntrl.c:529](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/bk_wifi_driver/wdrv_cntrl.c:529) already translates both IPC event IDs and posts `EVENT_WIFI_STA_CONNECTED`/`DISCONNECTED`.

**AP DHCP**

Change the VNET connect branch in [AP bk_netif.c:91](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/bk_netif/bk_netif.c:91):

```c
#if CONFIG_WIFI_VNET_AP_IPV4
	sta_ip_mode_set(1);
	sta_ip_down();
	sta_ip_start();
#else
	/* existing CP connect_ind -> static-IP setup */
#endif
```

Also compile `netif_vnet_fill_ip4_from_connect_ind()` only under `!CONFIG_WIFI_VNET_AP_IPV4` at [AP bk_netif.c:56](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/bk_netif/bk_netif.c:56). AP DHCP then owns address, gateway, and DNS; AP lwIP naturally owns TCP/UDP.

**Buffer Copy**

Keep `CONFIG_CONTROLLER_AP_BUFFER_COPY=n` on both cores. AP lwIP currently uses SRAM (`CONFIG_LWIP_MEM_LIBC_MALLOC_USE_PSRAM=n`), and [wdrv_main.h:20](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/bk_wifi_driver/wdrv_main.h:20) explicitly couples buffer-copy mode to PSRAM. Enabling it would add TX clones and require a larger controller queue without helping this ownership split.

**Hidden Consequences**

- `BK_EVT_IPV4_IND` will no longer occur because CP never obtains a lease. Consumers must use AP’s `EVENT_NETIF_GOT_IP4`.
- CP WLAN-status/IP commands will report link state but zero/stale IP, gateway, and DNS. Query AP `bk_netif` instead.
- CP IP services such as ping, iperf, MQTT, webclient, NTP, keepalive, and IP-based OTA cease to work by design.
- AP static-IP setup remains legacy and currently mirrors configuration to CP. If static IP is required, retain the config locally on AP and bypass `STA_SET_IP4_STATIC_IP`.
- The unconditional IPv4/ARP forwarding described above affects all VNET roles. If SoftAP/P2P must remain CP-owned, gate it with `cif_vif_to_netif_wire(vif) == 0`; if AP owns those roles too, CP `uap_ip_*`/P2P IP startup must also be suppressed.
- Disabling CP periodic ARP refresh may reduce a Wi-Fi power-save optimization, but avoids stale CP ARP. Normal AP ARP resolution remains intact.
